findings.claim: The new early `return null` when `suppressSourceGeneration is true` skips the whole TypeCollector analysis for the type. A `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` class with a public property that has no [Key] or [IgnoreMember] therefore gets no MsgPack004. MsgPack003/005 for its member types are also dropped, because the members are never visited. This is the opposite of the acceptance criterion that the analyzer still reports MsgPack0xx diagnostics with SuppressSourceGeneration = true. L14 only exempts the generation-only rules (011, 016, 017), not 003/004/005.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerReceiptTests.MissingKeyOnSuppressedType_ReportsMsgPack004 and MemberTypeNotMessagePackObject_OnSuppressedType_ReportsMsgPack003. On head, no MsgPack004/MsgPack003 diagnostic is produced, so both tests fail.

findings.claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards silently discard the second member when two members share the same int or string key. Before, `Add` threw, so the generator or analyzer failure was visible. Now the generated formatter is produced without that member, and no diagnostic in this hunk flags the duplicate, so the member's data is never serialized. The dynamic resolver throws on duplicate keys at run time. The early return above means these guards only run for generated (non-suppressed) types, so this does not help the reported bug and adds a silent-drop path.

receipt_plan.detail: In TypeCollector.cs lines 1029-1032, 1045-1048, 1169-1172 and 1185-1188, a duplicate key now falls through without a diagnostic. Compile `[MessagePackObject] public class C { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} [Key(0)] public int B {get;set;} }` with the generator. If no duplicate-key diagnostic exists elsewhere, the generated formatter omits B.
